hints: Use a balanced sequence tree that can isolate a substring by position.
Reversing a whole subtree can be represented by a pending flag.
Swap children and propagate reversal lazily only when visiting a node.
analogy: A label on a ribbon says its whole piece is flipped; individual sections are flipped only when needed.
example: Reversing positions 2 through 4 of ABCDE gives ADCBE.
algorithm: Use an implicit treap with subtree sizes and lazy reversal flags. Split before a and after b, toggle reversal on the middle subtree, and merge the pieces back. Push pending flags before descending or splitting, then output an in-order traversal.
correctness: A lazy reversal swaps the order of the two child sequences and reverses each child; pushing the flag preserves that meaning. Splits isolate the requested substring, so each operation produces exactly its reversal.
complexity: For length n and m operations, expected O(n+m log n) time and O(n) space with linear-time construction.
